title: Yara and the Garden
premise: Paloma Crane has spent her whole life in the Godless Valley, where her mercenary company's silent god cannot reach and magic cannot follow — a safe, dull exile she resents. When a century-old prophecy book surfaces naming 'the Crane of the dateless night' as the unmaker of crowns, she is dragged out of the valley into a world of living magic, where the rightful king Aldric wears a crown that has grown into his skull and whispers with another's voice. Guided by Yara, a garden-witch whose orchard grows memories instead of fruit, Paloma must gather the free cities' fractured allies before the usurper's armies march. In the end, Paloma learns the prophecy was written by her own grandmother, who bound the god's silence to protect her line — and that unbinding the king means unbinding her god, choosing a dangerous, mortal freedom over divine safety, and planting the crown itself in Yara's garden so it can grow into something new.
about_author: Hazel Quintana is a former botanist who traded greenhouse work for manuscript pages, and her love of slow-growing things still shapes everything she writes. She lives at the edge of an old orchard with two opinionated cats and a stubborn belief that stories, like gardens, reward patience.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Nothing Follows
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A routine escort job through the Godless Valley shows Paloma's competence and restlessness; her company prays to a god that hasn't answered in a century, and only she still bothers. Beat: restless discontent beneath competent routine, ending with a stranger arriving carrying a book that makes her name burn on the page.

chapters.title: A Date Written a Century Ago
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The stranger, a dying archivist, shows her the prophecy book: tonight's exact date, her description, and a command to unbind the king. She laughs it off — until the valley's magic-dead air shudders and the book pulls her bodily through. Beat: disbelief curdling into terror as the one safe place in the world expels her.

chapters.title: The Orchard of Remembered Fruit
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara, a garden-witch tending an orchard that grows memories, finds a half-dead mercenary collapsed among her pear trees and tastes the stranger's memories in the fruit. Beat: cautious compassion; Yara recognizes the prophecy's arrival means her long hiding is over, and chooses to shelter Paloma anyway.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Recovering in the orchard, Paloma eats a memory-fruit by accident and experiences her grandmother's life — including a glimpse of the prophecy book being written. She realizes the archivist was sent by her own bloodline. Beat: shaken wonder turning to suspicion about what her family has hidden from her.

chapters.title: The Crown That Whispers
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. In the occupied capital, Aldric fights a losing war for his own mind against the crown fused to his skull, which speaks with the usurper's honeyed voice. Beat: horror and dwindling hope; he clings to small memories of his mother's garden to stay himself.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Hiding
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Usurper scouts burn a neighboring farm hunting prophecy-bearers; Yara uproots a memory-tree to hide Paloma inside its roots. They flee together. Beat: fear and resolve; Yara's first act of open defiance, and the beginning of the two women's wary partnership.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Disagree
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the free city of Vessa, Paloma petitions the merchant council for aid and is mocked — a godless mercenary and a hedge-witch against an army. She wins a grudging hearing by fighting their champion to a draw. Beat: humiliation transmuted into fierce credibility; first taste of leadership.

chapters.title: Lessons in Living Magic
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara teaches Paloma the basics of garden-magic, but Paloma's god-touched blood makes plants grow wrong — too fast, too hungry. Beat: intimacy and frustration; Yara sees the god's silence isn't absence but a binding, and keeps the discovery to herself, planting the seed of later betrayal and trust.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Mercy
chapters.summary: The usurper's POV. General Sarel Vane, who wears the usurper's colors but not his heart, takes a free city by offering generous terms — then watches the crown's agents slaughter the surrendered garrison anyway. Beat: moral horror; Sarel begins quietly questioning whose war she is fighting.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Debts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma calls in every mercenary debt she's owed to raise a ragged host, including her estranged former commander, Brannoc, who blames her grandmother for the company's godless exile. Beat: bitter reconciliation; Brannoc joins but reveals the company's founding oath was sworn to keep the Cranes watched, not protected.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath the Palace
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara infiltrates the capital's dead royal garden and finds it still faintly alive beneath the flagstones — the crown's power is rooted there. She makes contact with Aldric through a surviving rosebush. Beat: clandestine hope; the first direct link between the rescuers and the king.

chapters.title: What My Grandmother Bound
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following the archivist's letters, Paloma finds her grandmother's hidden workshop and learns the truth: the Crane line bound the god's silence to hide the one weapon that can unmake the crown — and the binding is killing Paloma the longer she stays in magic's reach. Beat: devastating revelation; her safety was always a slow sacrifice.

chapters.title: The March on Vessa
chapters.summary: Sarel's POV. The usurper's main army marches on Vessa; Sarel sabotages supply lines in secret while the crown's agents grow suspicious. Beat: escalating dread; Sarel's defection becomes inevitable but must wait for the right moment.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Broken Bridge
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma's ragged host holds the bridge into Vessa against overwhelming odds; Yara's memory-trees turn the field into a labyrinth of the usurper's own regrets. Victory, but Brannoc falls. Beat: triumph shadowed by grief; Paloma learns command costs what she cannot pay back.

chapters.title: The Crown Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The crown, wounded by Yara's garden-magic, drops its mask and reveals it is a fragment of the bound god, corrupted by a century of imprisonment and hunger. It offers Aldric his mind back if he delivers Paloma. Beat: temptation and clarity; Aldric understands the enemy is also a prisoner, and refuses.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Choice
chapters.summary: Sarel's POV. Exposed as a saboteur, Sarel escapes the usurper's camp with the army's true battle-plans and defects to Paloma, offering them at knifepoint. Beat: tense redemption; Paloma must decide whether to trust the woman who burned Vessa's sister-city, and chooses to.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Heart
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The allies assault the capital while Sarel's plans let them bypass the walls. Paloma fights through the crown's corrupted servants toward the throne room, her god-touched blood burning her from inside as the binding frays. Beat: desperate momentum; the cost of the prophecy coming due in her veins.

chapters.title: Unbinding the King
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the throne room, Yara and Paloma reach Aldric, but the crown-god fragment offers Paloma her god's voice back — everything she has prayed a century for — in exchange for walking away. Paloma, weeping, chooses Aldric's freedom over her faith. Beat: the emotional climax; grief and love in the same breath.

chapters.title: What Wears a Crown
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The unbinding: Yara grafts the crown's root into living wood while Paloma holds the screaming god-fragment with her bare hands, and Aldric tears it free. The fragment, uncorrupted by soil and sunlight, speaks its first honest words — a blessing, not a command. Beat: catharsis through pain; power surrendered rather than seized.

chapters.title: The Usurper Unmasked
chapters.summary: Sarel's POV. With the crown's power broken, the usurper's armies collapse; Sarel arrests him with his own honor guard. The usurper was never more than the crown's first victim, hollowed into a puppet. Beat: grim justice; Sarel refuses a title, asking instead to be sent home to bury her dead.

chapters.title: The Orchard of New Fruit
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Spring in the restored royal garden: the crown, planted, has grown into a small tree that bears no power, only shade. Aldric rules cautiously with Sarel and the free cities as equals. Beat: quiet hope; institutions mended like grafts, imperfect and alive.

chapters.title: Yara and the Garden
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma, her binding dissolved, finally hears her god — a single, ordinary word of welcome, no commands. She chooses to stay in the valley's edge with Yara, planting the memory-orchard's next generation, and writes the final page of the prophecy book herself: blank. Beat: peace earned, not given; the future unwritten.
